questions.question: What are called 'Kitchen of cells'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chloroplast**__.

__**Explanation-**__

 
• **Chloroplast** is called the** 'Kitchen of cell'**.

• It is the** site of photosynthesis**.
 
• Chloroplasts are the **green plastids** that occur in all the green parts of the flower.
 
• Green plastids containing chlorophyll are called **chloroplasts**.

questions.question: The organsims which lack a nuclear membrane are called
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prokaryotes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In some organisms like bacteria, the nuclear region of the cell may be poorly defined due to the absence of a nuclear membrane.
 
• Such an undefined nuclear region containing only nucleic acids is called a **nucleoid**.
 
• Such** organisms, whose cells lack a nuclear membrane, are called prokaryotes **(Pro = primitive or primary; karyote » karyon = nucleus).
 
• Organisms with cells having a nuclear membrane are called **eukaryotes**. 
 
• Prokaryotic cells also lack most of the other cytoplasmic organelles present in eukaryotic cells.
 
• Many of the functions of such organelles are also performed by poorly organised parts of the cytoplasm.

questions.question: Evolutionary history of an organism is known as _______________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phylogeny.**__

__**Concept:**__

__
 
• **Evolution **is the gradual and continuous process of change that occurs over a period of time, due to slight variations in genetic compositions as well as changes in the environment, which leads to the formation of new species

**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **Phylogeny:** It is the study of the development of an organism through various generations during the process of evolution or in other words,** it is the evolutionary history of an organism**. The phylogenetic relationships are represented in the form of a **phylogenetic tree (cladogram)**, which shows how one taxon is related to another taxon. The phylogenetic tree diagram is based on molecular sequencing data analyses. Character or trait is the unit of data used in the phylogenetic.

• Ontogeny is the study of the origination and development of an organism. It covers the course of development of an individual organism. It covers the study beginning from the time of fertilization and includes all the developmental events at the time of birth and thereafter also.
 
• **Ancestry**: It is the study of primitive ancestors of the existing species of an organism.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Mitochondria is INCORRECT?

options.text: ATP generating chemical reactions get enhanced by the deeply folded surface area of the mitochondria.
The body uses energy stored in ATP for making new chemical compounds and for mechanical work.
Mitochondria are not capable of making their own proteins.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria are not capable of making their own proteins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mitochondria are indeed capable of making their own proteins.** They contain their own DNA and ribosomes which allow them to synthesize certain proteins independently.
 
• The mitochondrial inner membrane is extensively folded into structures known as cristae, which increase the surface area available for ATP-generating chemical reactions.
 
• The energy stored in ATP is used by the body for various processes, including the synthesis of new chemical compounds and mechanical work.
 
• **Mitochondria have a double-membrane structure.** The outer membrane is smooth, while the inner membrane is folded into cristae.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitochondria**

 
 
• Mitochondria are known as the powerhouses of the cell because they generate most of the cell's supply of ATP, used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• They are unique in having their own genome, which is similar to bacterial genomes, and they reproduce independently of the cell in which they reside.
 
• The double-membrane structure of mitochondria consists of an outer membrane and a highly convoluted inner membrane, the latter being the site of the electron transport chain and ATP synthesis.
 
• The inner membrane folds over many times to create layered structures called cristae. The increased surface area of these cristae enhances the mitochondrion's ability to produce ATP.
 
 
 
• **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)**
 
 
• ATP is the energy currency of the cell, providing the energy needed for many biochemical cellular processes including muscle contraction and protein synthesis.
 
• It is produced primarily in the mitochondria through a process known as oxidative phosphorylation, which occurs along the inner mitochondrial membrane.
 
 
 
• **Protein Synthesis in Mitochondria**
 
 
• Mitochondria have their own ribosomes and DNA, which enable them to produce some of their own proteins independently of the cell's nuclear DNA.
 
• The mitochondrial DNA encodes for a small number of proteins essential for the organelle’s function, particularly those involved in the electron transport chain.

questions.question: What is the cell wall of a plant made of ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cellulose**__.

__
 
• Plant cell walls are primarily made of cellulose.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Cellulose is the most abundant macromolecule on Earth.
 
 
• Cellulose fibers are long, linear polymers of hundreds of glucose molecules.
 
• These fibres aggregate into bundles of about 40, which are called microfibrils.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Carbohydrates are the sugars, starches, and fibres found in fruits, grains, vegetables, and milk products.
 
 
• A carbohydrate is a biomolecule consisting of carbon (C), hydrogen (H), and oxygen (O) atoms.
 
 
 
• Lipids are molecules that contain hydrocarbons and make up the building blocks of the structure and function of living cells.
 
 
• A lipid is a biomolecule that is soluble in nonpolar solvents.
 
 
 
• A lipoprotein is a biochemical assembly whose primary function is to transport hydrophobic lipid also known as fat molecules in water, as in blood plasma or other extracellular fluids.
 
 
• It consists of a Triglyceride and Cholesterol centre, surrounded by a phospholipid outer shell, with the hydrophilic portions oriented outward towards the surrounding water and lipophilic portions oriented inward toward the lipid centre.

questions.question: The number of chromosomes in a normal human body cell is __________,
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**46**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **chromosome **is the **fibrous nodules found in the cells** of **all flora and fauna, which determine and transmit **all the genetic properties. 
 
• The number of **chromosomes in each species remains fixed**.
 
• The main function of the **chromosome is to carry genes**.
 
• **Chromosomes are like long strands of DNA**, consisting of many genes.
 
• Humans have** 23 pairs of chromosomes(23 x 2 = 46) **and a set of them are inherited from each parent.
 
• **Females have two 'X' chromosomes, while males have one 'X' and one 'Y' chromosome each**.

questions.question: _________ are known as the protein factory of the cell.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ribosomes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ribosomes are known as the **protein factories of the cell** because they are responsible for synthesizing proteins by translating messenger RNA (mRNA).
 
• They are found in both **prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells**, either floating freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum.
 
• Ribosomes are composed of **ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins**, forming two subunits: one small and one large.
 
• Ribosomes attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum specialize in producing proteins for **secretion or membrane integration**, while free ribosomes synthesize proteins used within the cell.
 
• Protein synthesis in ribosomes is an essential process for cell growth, repair, and enzymatic function.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER):**

 
 
• The ER is classified into two types: **Rough ER** (with ribosomes attached) and **Smooth ER** (without ribosomes).
 
• Rough ER is involved in protein synthesis, while Smooth ER is associated with lipid synthesis and detoxification processes.
 
 
 
• **Nucleus:**
 
 
• The nucleus is the control center of the cell, containing the cell’s genetic material (DNA).
 
• It regulates cellular activities by controlling gene expression and coordinating cell division.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria:**
 
 
• Known as the **powerhouses of the cell**, mitochondria are responsible for producing energy in the form of ATP through cellular respiration.
 
• They have their own DNA and are believed to have originated from endosymbiotic bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Protein Synthesis:**
 
 
• Protein synthesis occurs in two main stages: **transcription** (DNA to mRNA) and **translation** (mRNA to protein).
 
• Ribosomes play a crucial role in the translation process by decoding the mRNA sequence and assembling amino acids into polypeptide chains.

questions.question: Plasma membrane is made up of ______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both proteins and lipids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The plasma membrane is primarily composed of a bilayer of lipids, mainly phospholipids, with embedded proteins.
 
• Phospholipids form the fundamental structure, creating a semi-permeable membrane.
 
• Proteins in the plasma membrane serve various functions including transport, signal transduction, and acting as enzymes.
 
• The fluid mosaic model describes the plasma membrane as a dynamic arrangement of phospholipids and proteins.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phospholipids**:

 
 
• Composed of a hydrophilic (water-attracting) "head" and two hydrophobic (water-repelling) "tails".
 
• They arrange themselves into a bilayer in aqueous environments, with heads facing outward and tails inward.
 
 
 
• **Integral Proteins**:
 
 
• Span the entire membrane and are involved in transport and communication across the membrane.
 
 
 
• **Peripheral Proteins**:
 
 
• Located on the surface of the membrane and play a role in cell signaling and maintaining the cell's shape.
 
 
 
• **Cholesterol**:
 
 
• Present within the lipid bilayer, it helps to stabilize the fluidity of the membrane.
 
 
 
• **Glycoproteins and Glycolipids**:
 
 
• Carbohydrate chains attached to proteins and lipids, involved in cell recognition and signaling.

questions.question: In the division of the division, a parent cell is divided into _____________ for the preparation of mass cells.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Two Similar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During cell division, a parent cell divides to form two similar daughter cells.
 
• This process ensures that each **daughter cell receives an identical set of genetic material** from the parent cell.
 
• Cell division is crucial for growth, repair, and reproduction in living organisms.
 
• There are two main types of cell division: **mitosis and meiosis**.
 
• Mitosis results in two identical daughter cells, while meiosis results in four genetically diverse cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitosis**

 
 
• It is a type of cell division that results in two daughter cells each having the same number and kind of chromosomes as the parent nucleus.
 
• Mitosis is essential for growth and repair in multicellular organisms.
 
• It consists of several stages: **prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase**.
 
 
 
• **Meiosis**
 
 
• Meiosis is a specialized form of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half, resulting in four daughter cells, each genetically distinct from the parent cell.
 
• It is crucial for sexual reproduction and genetic diversity.
 
• Meiosis consists of two consecutive divisions: **meiosis I and meiosis II**.

questions.question: Omnis cellula - e - cellula was proposed by:
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **Omnis cellula - e - cellula** was proposed by** Rudolf Virchow **in the year 1855. He was the first person to explain that cells divided and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells.
 
• He modified the hypothesis of **Schleiden **and **Schwann** to give the cell theory a final shape. Cell theory as understood today is:

 
• All living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells.
 
• All cells arise from pre-existing cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Robert Hooke**: He was the first person to discover cell. He dissected the Oak and saw it under the microscope, he observed honeycomb-like boxes or compartments. These boxes were empty in the middle and surrounded by a layer in the periphery. Robert hook named these compartments as cellulae, which are today known as cells. 
 
• **Matthias Schleiden **was a German botanist who examined a large number of plants and observed that all plants are composed of different kinds of cells that form the tissues of the plant.
 
• **Theodore Schwann** was a British Zoologist who studied different types of animal cells and reported that cells had a thin outer layer which is today known as the **‘plasma membrane’.** He also concluded, based on his studies on plant tissues, that the presence of cell wall is a unique character of the plant cells.
 
• **Schleiden** and** Schwann **together formulated the **cell theory.**

• **Mitochondria **produce the energy necessary for the cell's survival and functioning. 
 
• By the** chemical reactions**,** mitochondria break down glucose** into an **energy molecule **known as **adenosine triphosphate (ATP)**, which is used to fuel various other cellular processes.
 
• Mitochondria are **membrane-bound cell organelles (mitochondrion, singular)** that generate most of the **chemical energy needed to power the cell's biochemical reactions. **
 
• **Chemical energy produced by the mitochondria is stored in a small molecule called adenosine triphosphate (ATP).**
